$comment: Generated from the program by opensloper-cli doc drape.schema.json; do not edit it by hand.
title: OpenSloper drape file (.sdrape)
description: Made by opensloper-drape: the pieces of one or more patterns placed round a body in 3D, for draping in Blender. Positions are in mm: x to the body's left, y towards its back, z up, the body facing -y with its feet at z = 0.

format.description: What the file is; a file with another value does not load

version.description: The version of the format, from 1. The apps read every older version and always write the current one; they refuse a file newer than they know

units.description: Always mm: values in this file are millimetres

nextId.description: The next source ID to hand out

sources.description: The patterns placed, each with the measurements to draw it with

id.description: The source's ID, which placements refer to

pattern.description: The pattern file, relative to the layout's folder

measurementFile.description: The measurement file, relative to the layout's folder; the pattern's own when left out

size.description: The size, for a size table; its first size when left out

body.description: The body the pieces are placed on

kind.description: measurements: a generic body built from a measurement set; none: no body, for accessories

measurementFile.description: The body's measurement file, relative to the drape file's folder; the first source's when left out

size.description: The body's size, for a size table; the first source's when left out

gap.description: How far pieces are placed off the body and apart across a seam

placements.description: Where each copy of each piece is placed; a copy not listed is left out

source.description: The source the piece is from

piece.description: The piece's ID in that source's pattern

copy.description: Which copy, from 1, for a piece cut more than once

position.description: Where the piece's anchor goes: x, y and z. The anchor is the middle of its grainline, else the middle of its seam line's extent

rotation.description: The turns in degrees about x, then y, then z, anticlockwise looking from the positive end of each axis: Blender's XYZ Euler angles. Unturned, a piece stands upright facing -y, as drawn
